question: Session 2 makes the extension depend on python -m ai_router.modules, but nothing guarantees a compatible dabbler-ai-router is installed in the project venv. Where does the install guarantee go, given the operator publishes to PyPI and the Marketplace immediately after Set 122 lands?
decision: Add a Session 4 to Set 122 for the router-install guarantee, and gate the set (and therefore both releases) on it.

options.option: Fold the install guarantee into Session 2
options.consequence: Session 2 already carries five launchers, the moduleAuthoring.ts lifecycle deletion, the echo surface, the cancelLifecycle.ts:296 fix, the menu entry and a full Playwright run; adding provisioning and an L-079-3 cold-start dogfood breaks the 3-work-step session-size cap.

options.option: Add Session 4 for it and gate the release on that session
options.consequence: Session 2 stays inside the size cap. Session 4 owns the version floor, an upgrade-capable install, a post-install capability probe on the same venv interpreter, failure gating before any Python-backed module mutation, the retryability fix, and the true cold-start dogfood. Neither release publishes until it is green.

options.option: Minimum in Session 2, defer the cold-start dogfood to a later set
options.consequence: Ships the fix but skips the walk L-079-3 requires of any set shipping provisioning - the exact place silent fail-open paths hide.

options.option: Ship Set 122 as specified and handle provisioning in a new set before publishing
options.consequence: Set 122 could land and be published before the guarantee exists, breaking module commands for every existing project whose venv holds 0.34.0.

evidence: PyPI dabbler-ai-router latest is 0.34.0; pyproject.toml stages 1.0.0.

aiRouterInstall.ts:431 install mode runs a plain pip install (no --upgrade), which pip reports as already-satisfied against an existing 0.34.0 venv; only update mode passes --upgrade --force-reinstall.

gitScaffold.ts:145 creates docs/modules.yaml BEFORE the install at :148, and :530 gates default-module creation on the manifest having been created IN THAT CALL - so a failed install cannot be recovered by re-running setup once that path is Python-backed.
Session 2 deletes scaffoldNewModule, which gitScaffold.ts calls, so it must touch the provisioning path regardless.
release_ordering: Operator-executed and unchanged by this decision: publish dabbler-ai-router first, confirm the wheel is live on PyPI, then publish the extension.
